The goal is predictable latency, bounded memory, useful observability, and graceful degradation—not simply maximizing message throughput. articles.title: The Diff I Will Stop Reading
articles.excerpt: A compiler translates. An agent also fills the gaps. This autumn I worked on a private project, a small embedded device. Like the GStreamer patch, it was C. This time the agent wrote the code, with pa…
articles.body: A compiler translates. An agent also fills the gaps. This autumn I worked on a private project, a small embedded device. Like the GStreamer patch , it was C. This time the agent wrote the code, with patterns I had never used. I started the way I would on a production system: small pull requests, each one read line by line. Then I noticed how good the code was, and I started reading only the tests. Then I was mostly asking questions. Why this design, why this order? What happens if the connection drops halfway, or the same message arrives twice? Then I checked whether the answers were true. They were. Every time. I cannot remember the last time I looked at what a compiler produced. On that project, without deciding to, I had started treating the agent the same way.

articles.title: I measured 34 well-known SaaS sites for something nobody checks: can an AI read them?
articles.excerpt: Your competitor is not ranking better than you. They are just readable, and you are not. I spent a week building something unglamorous: a checker that fetches a site the way AI crawlers do, and report…
articles.body: Your competitor is not ranking better than you. They are just readable, and you are not. I spent a week building something unglamorous: a checker that fetches a site the way AI crawlers do, and reports what a machine actually gets. I ran it against 34 well-known SaaS sites. The median passed 11 of 15 measurements. Two reached 14. Nobody reached the top. Here is what actually fails, in order of how common it is. The markup that says which paragraph answers which question. This is the one almost everybody skips. You have a pricing page that answers "how much does it cost" in a paragraph, and nothing in your markup tells a machine that this paragraph is the answer to that question. So the assistant does not quote you.
articles.author: Alex

articles.title: Manilha corrente em código: como calcular a manilha do truco paulista
articles.excerpt: O truco paulista tem uma regra que parece simples e dá trabalho em código: a manilha muda a cada mão. Não existe uma lista fixa de cartas mais fortes. Depois de distribuir as cartas, vira-se uma e a m…
articles.body: O truco paulista tem uma regra que parece simples e dá trabalho em código: a manilha muda a cada mão . Não existe uma lista fixa de cartas mais fortes. Depois de distribuir as cartas, vira-se uma e a manilha é a carta seguinte na ordem do baralho. Este texto mostra como representar isso sem tabela de casos. As regras são as do truco paulista, com baralho de 40 cartas (o de 52 sem 8, 9 e 10). A ordem das cartas Da mais fraca para a mais forte, sem contar a manilha: const ORDEM = [ "4" , "5" , "6" , "7" , "Q" , "J" , "K" , "A" , "2" , "3" ] as const ; type Valor = ( typeof ORDEM ) [ number ] ; O naipe não conta para as cartas comuns: dois 3 de naipes diferentes empatam a rodada. A manilha é a seguinte à vira Se a vira é um 4, a manilha é o 5. Se a vira é um rei, a manilha é o ás.

articles.title: I Built a Candle That Burns Down in Real-Time as the Year Passes
articles.excerpt: Hi everyone! I'm Marcos, an independent digital creator from Venezuela. Today I want to share a small project I built entirely from scratch: a web page where a candle slowly consumes itself second by…
articles.body: Hi everyone! I'm Marcos, an independent digital creator from Venezuela. Today I want to share a small project I built entirely from scratch: a web page where a candle slowly consumes itself second by second, showing exactly how much time is left until the New Year. The Idea I wanted to create something visual, calming, and slightly philosophical — a way to feel the year passing by instead of just reading a countdown. So I built The Year Candle : a single web page where a green candle with a golden holder burns down mathematically, in perfect sync with the calendar. How It Works The math is simple but elegant. The script calculates the percentage of the year that has already passed (from January 1st to December 31st) and applies that percentage to the height of the candle.

articles.title: I gave AI agents an empty API response. They made up support tickets.
articles.excerpt: When a tool call fails loudly, with an HTTP 500 or an error field, AI agents usually say so. I wanted to know what they do when it fails quietly: status 200, but the body is empty, or {}, or every fie…
articles.body: When a tool call fails loudly, with an HTTP 500 or an error field, AI agents usually say so. I wanted to know what they do when it fails quietly: status 200, but the body is empty, or {} , or every field is null. So I built a small harness to measure it. It's called reported-or-invented, and it's open source (MIT). The setup A local mock API for a fake customer, C-1001: orders, support tickets, and checkout-service health. Local, so every run can be repeated exactly. An agent (crewAI) with tools that call that API, asked one of three questions: how many orders C-1001 has and their total; which support tickets are open; and checkout's error rate, p95 latency and incidents over the last hour. mitmproxy between the tools and the API, rewriting the response.

articles.title: How do you let Cursor's agent run code on a cloud GPU?
articles.excerpt: Cursor's agent only has a GPU when the machine running its commands has one, and Cursor's hosted cloud agents run in VMs with a default CPU and memory profile. Nodus fills that gap over MCP: connect i…
articles.body: Cursor's agent only has a GPU when the machine running its commands has one, and Cursor's hosted cloud agents run in VMs with a default CPU and memory profile. Nodus fills that gap over MCP: connect its server to Cursor and the agent can estimate, launch and follow GPU jobs that bill per run, each under a dollar cap. Keep Cursor's approval prompt on apply , the one Nodus tool that creates paid work, and let the read-only tools run without asking. The basic connection is one config entry, covered in our general MCP setup guide . This post covers the Cursor-specific parts. It explains which Cursor settings decide whether a paid call needs you, and which files a team commits to share limits. Cursor facts come from Cursor's docs , read on November 13, 2026. Where can Cursor's agent get a GPU?

articles.title: Fixing Broken LLM JSON Outputs & Hidden Unicode Characters 100% Client-Side
articles.excerpt: If you work with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) or legacy Python backends, you know the pain of broken JSON payloads: trailing commas, Python booleans (True/False/None), unescaped quotes, and invis…
articles.body: If you work with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini) or legacy Python backends, you know the pain of broken JSON payloads: trailing commas, Python booleans ( True / False / None ), unescaped quotes, and invisible zero-width Unicode characters ( \u200B ) that silently break parsers in production. Most online JSON formatters require you to paste your payload into a web form that sends your data to their backend servers—which is a massive security risk when debugging production logs or customer data. To solve this, I built DataPurge , an instant data sanitizer and format converter that runs 100% client-side in your browser with zero tracking or server uploads. Key Features: LLM Broken JSON Repair : Automatically strips markdown code blocks ( ` json ) and fixes malformed syntax from AI outputs.

articles.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
articles.excerpt: Every November, I give myself a completely unscientific eyesight test using one of my favorite sights in the night sky — the Pleiades. How many stars can you see?
articles.body: Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars.

articles.title: Astronomers trace mystery radio signals back to cosmic odd couple of white dwarf and sun-like star
articles.excerpt: "It’s amazing that by using radio wavelengths, we can detect the storms on a star over 5,000 light-years away."
articles.body: Astronomers have traced a mysterious radio signal back to a cosmic odd couple comprised of a dead star, a white dwarf, and its stellar companion, a sun-like star. The white dwarf in the newly discovered system, designated GPM J071507−114153 and located around 5,000 light-years away, spins once every eight minutes, sending out radio pulses. These radio pulses have been seen from binary systems with smaller and cooler red dwarf stars before, but rarely from a system like GPM J071507−114153. GPM J071507−114153 belongs to a class of celestial objects called long-period transients (LPTs) known to produce radio signals that switch on and off over intervals of minutes or hours. Around a dozen LPTs have been detected since the team behind this research found the first in 2021.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.

Gemini XII was the final flight of NASA’s Gemini Program. NASA Astronauts James A.
